guideTitle: The Best Rolling CPU Stands and Tower Carts
metaTitle: Best Rolling CPU Stands and PC Tower Carts (2026)
metaDescription: We compared rolling CPU stands, from low adjustable-width dollies to desk-height ZUAVIALA carts with a power outlet, on fit, height, casters and features.
introParagraphs: A rolling CPU stand gets a desktop tower off the carpet and lets you pull it out to reach cables or clean. There are two kinds here: low stands, a few inches high, that sit under the desk; and taller ZUAVIALA carts that raise the tower toward desk height and add surface space.
For the low stands, compare the width range with your case and look for side rails. None of the listings here state a weight capacity, so check your tower's weight with the seller if it is heavy.
Our comparison is based on published specifications and price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $15 to $46 at the time of writing.

best-rolling-cpu-stands-1.summary: A metal tower cart adjustable from 21.34 to 28.3 inches high that doubles as extra desk space.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-1.description:
The ZUAVIALA is the pick if you want the tower within reach: a metal cart that adjusts from 21.34 to 28.3 inches high with a knob, bringing the PC close to desk height and adding surface space beside the desk.

That makes ports and power buttons easier to reach and keeps the tower away from floor dust.

It takes more floor space than a low stand, and the listing does not state a weight capacity or caster details.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-1.bestFor: Desks where the tower should sit beside you, not under the desk.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-1.skipIf: You want the tower hidden under the desk; a low stand suits that.

best-rolling-cpu-stands-2.summary: An adjustable-width metal and plastic stand with four casters for about $15.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-2.description:
This mobile stand is the budget pick: adjustable width, four caster wheels and a metal and PS plastic frame designed to work on hard floors and carpet, for about $15 at the time of writing.

The listing does not give the width range or a weight capacity, so check your case size.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-2.skipIf: You have a heavy tower; choose a steel stand.

best-rolling-cpu-stands-3.summary: An adjustable-width stand that lifts the PC 1.75 inches off carpet.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-3.description:
This PC stand lifts the tower 1.75 inches off the floor, which the seller says protects it from dust, spills, carpet fibers and moisture, with adjustable width for most cases and casters for mobility.

It costs about $16 at the time of writing. The width range and weight rating are not stated.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-3.skipIf: You want side rails; the Hovadova has them.

best-rolling-cpu-stands-4.summary: An unbranded stand with side rails and four swivel wheels.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-4.description:
This stand has protective rails on both sides to stop the case sliding off and four 360-degree wheels, for about $25 at the time of writing.

It lists no dimensions or weight capacity, and the brand is not named.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-4.skipIf: The Hovadova has rails and stated widths for less.

best-rolling-cpu-stands-5.summary: The ZUAVIALA tower cart with a built-in power outlet.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-5.description:
This ZUAVIALA cart adds a power outlet to the desk-height tower cart design, so you can plug in the PC or accessories at the cart.

It is the most expensive option here at about $46 at the time of writing. The listing does not state surge protection, height range or weight capacity; the plain ZUAVIALA lists 21.34 to 28.3 inches.
specs: Surge protection and capacity: not stated
best-rolling-cpu-stands-5.bestFor: Setups where a nearby outlet is useful.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-5.skipIf: You do not need an outlet; the plain ZUAVIALA costs less.

best-rolling-cpu-stands-6.summary: A low-profile steel VIVO cart for mid-tower cases.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-6.description:
The VIVO mid-tower cart is a low-profile steel cart on four casters, from an established desk-accessory brand, for about $25 at the time of writing.

It is sized for mid-tower cases; the listing does not give dimensions or a weight capacity.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-6.skipIf: You have a full ATX tower; the larger VIVO fits it.

best-rolling-cpu-stands-7.summary: VIVO's larger steel cart for full ATX cases.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-7.description:
The larger VIVO cart is the same low-profile steel design sized for larger ATX towers, for about $30 at the time of writing.

The listing does not give dimensions or capacity, so confirm your case fits.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-7.skipIf: Your case is a mid-tower; the smaller VIVO costs less.

best-rolling-cpu-stands-8.summary: A Hovadova stand with side rails, 7.87–10.23 inches wide, for about $20.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-8.description:
The Hovadova is the low stand with the clearest specifications: 7.87 to 10.23 inches wide, 16.9 inches long, with side rails and a ventilated frame, for about $20 at the time of writing.

The listing does not state a weight capacity.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-8.bestFor: Standard towers within its width range.
best-rolling-cpu-stands-8.skipIf: Your case is wider than about 10 inches.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Low stands hide the tower under the desk; ZUAVIALA carts raise it toward desk height and add surface.
Measure your case's width and length. The Hovadova lists 7.87–10.23 inches wide; VIVO sells mid-tower and ATX sizes.
None of these listings state one. Confirm with the seller for a heavy tower.
Side rails help keep the case in place; casters ease cleaning and cable access.

faq.q: Why put a PC on a rolling stand?
faq.a: It keeps the tower off carpet and dust, helps airflow, and lets you roll it out to reach cables or clean.

faq.q: How much weight can these hold?
faq.a: None of the listings here state a capacity. Check with the seller for a heavy tower.
Compare your case's width and length with the stand's range, or choose a VIVO sized for mid-tower or ATX cases.

bottomLine: For a tower under the desk, the Hovadova is the low stand with the clearest specifications, and the VIVO carts suit mid-tower and large ATX cases from an established brand.
If you want the PC beside you at desk height, the ZUAVIALA cart does that and adds surface space, with a power-outlet version for a few dollars more.
